section: Educational Psychology · Ch13 — Bloom's Taxonomy (Complete 6 Levels)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A teacher asks students to read two different essays on the same topic and judge which one presents a more convincing argument, giving reasons for their choice. This task targets Bloom's (revised) level of:
explanation: Evaluate involves making judgments based on criteria/standards (judging which argument is more convincing, with reasons) — the second-highest level in Bloom's revised taxonomy, below only 'Create'.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch13 — Bloom's Taxonomy (Complete 6 Levels)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Arrange Bloom's revised taxonomy's six cognitive levels in correct order, from lowest to highest:

options.option_text: Remember → Understand → Apply → Analyse → Evaluate → Create
Create → Evaluate → Analyse → Apply → Understand → Remember
Understand → Remember → Create → Apply → Analyse → Evaluate
Apply → Remember → Understand → Create → Analyse → Evaluate

explanation: Bloom's revised taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001) orders cognitive levels: Remember (recall facts) → Understand (explain ideas) → Apply (use in new situations) → Analyse (draw connections) → Evaluate (justify a judgment) → Create (produce original work) — the highest level.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch13 — Bloom's Taxonomy (Complete 6 Levels)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student who can restate a scientific concept from the textbook in their own words, without merely reciting it verbatim, is operating at Bloom's level of:
explanation: 'Understand' involves explaining ideas/concepts in one's own words — a step beyond mere 'Remember' (verbatim recall), but not yet 'Analyse' (breaking into parts) or 'Create' (producing something new).
